chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about selling gold for dirhams, so he said: Send a messenger so he would fulfill its price for you, and he should be saying, 'Give and take', and your messenger would happen to be with him.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling gold for silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of 'qabd' (possession) in the exchange of gold for silver, a foundational principle for avoiding riba al-fadl. The Imam’s instruction to send a messenger who remains present until the full price is received highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on immediate physical or constructive possession to ensure the transaction is complete and free from uncertainty. This practical guidance underscores the importance of witnessing the actual transfer of value in commercial dealings.
